subject: Recap: Dedicated Capacity discovery — Fintechex (next steps & requirements)
thread_messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechex.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@fintechex.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Dedicated Capacity discovery — Fintechex (next steps & requirements)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap of what we heard and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points / goals
- High variability in inference demand with several predictable peaks at end of day and month-end reporting windows; current infra can't handle spikes without large cost increases.
- Need strict data isolation for PCI-scope models and prefer dedicated tenancy for inference stacks.
- Target P95 latency for inference should be < 400ms for typical user flows; batch jobs can be higher.
- Cost predictability is a key success metric — looking for committed capacity pricing with predictable TPS costs.

Current stack
- Model infra: in-house model serving on k8s using mixed-comp instance fleet (GPUs + CPU fallback).
- Orchestration: internal autoscaling using spot instances; no dedicated reserved GPU pool today.
- Security: SOC 2 in progress; they manage keys in KMS.

Success criteria (for initial Dedicated capacity POC)
- Reserved GPU pool that delivers predictable throughput for 500-1,000 TPS (peak) with P95 latency < 400ms.
- Strong network/VPC isolation and audit logs delivered to their SIEM.
- Ability to autoscale with defined burst policy (burst to on-demand capacity for up to 30% of peak for 10–30 minute windows).
- Cost estimate demonstrating 20–30% TCO improvement vs current spot-heavy fleet at expected utilization.

Dedicated fit details discussed
- Reserved GPU pools (8 A100-equivalent GPUs baseline discussed; customer may scale up).
- Throughput targets: baseline 500 TPS sustained, spikes to 1,000 TPS.
- Isolation: customer requires dedicated tenancy + VPC peering and customer-managed KMS keys.
- Autoscaling/burst: want automatic burst to on-demand capacity for 30% additional TPS; acceptable cold-start penalty < 2s for scale-up paths.

Action items / next steps
1) Marissa / Redwood to share: preliminary reserved-capacity pricing, deployment architecture diagram, and SOC2 evidence pack (attached). 
2) Schedule technical deep-dive with Rishi (solutions/infra) and Fintechex infra team to validate autoscaling signals and KV/cache behavior.
3) Customer to confirm expected steady-state TPS and peak durations (hourly profile) so we can size cache and batching policies.
4) Tentative pilot: 2–4 week dedicated pool with monitoring and cost telemetry.

Attached: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf (pdf), security-overview.pdf (pdf), deployment-arch-diagram.png (image)

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated Capacity discovery — Fintechex (next steps & requirements)

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures things well. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For throughput, our internal dashboards show sustained periods around ~600 TPS with short spikes up to ~900–1,000 TPS; peaks last 5–20 minutes.
- Latency: P95 targets of < 400ms are correct for interactive flows. For some batch scoring jobs we can tolerate higher.
- For sizing: can you provide an initial price for a committed pool equivalent to 8 A100s and an option for 12 A100s? Also include estimated overage/burst pricing.

We'd like to get Rishi on a call with our infra lead (Samir Patel) next week to go over autoscaling signals and network setup. Samir is available Wednesday 10–12 PST.

Appreciate the SOC2 pack — we'll review and share with security.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
CTO, Fintechex
alex.j@fintechex.com

-----Original Message-----
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 09:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated Capacity discovery — Fintechex (next steps & requirements)

Quick technical questions to prepare for the deep-dive:
1) Autoscaling signals — what metrics do you want us to use for scale decisions? CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, request rate, or a combination?
2) Burst policy — you mentioned 30% headroom. Is burst allowed to provision on-demand machines (i.e., non-reserved) and are there any procurement limitations?
3) KV cache — is cache warm-up acceptable at pilot start or do you need pre-warmed persistent caches?

Answers will help us propose batching and cache sizing; I can propose an autoscale policy template once we confirm.

-Rishi

-----Original Message-----
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechex.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@fintechex.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 11:15:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap: Dedicated Capacity discovery — Fintechex (next steps & requirements)

Rishi — good questions. Answers below:
1) Autoscaling signals: use request rate + GPU utilization. Our infra emits request rate at 1s granularity; queue length is less reliable.
2) Burst policy: yes, burst to on-demand/reserved-on-demand is ok; procurement requires we inform procurement for any long-running on-demand costs (beyond 6 hours). Short bursts (<= 30 minutes) are fine.
3) KV cache: would prefer pre-warmed cache for pilot for customer-facing flows; for longer batch jobs we can tolerate cold caches.

We'll confirm the steady-state hourly profile before the deep-dive.

Thanks,
Alex
